intended_object: The generator of the reduced zeroth singular homology of the two-point discrete space S⁰ = {false, true}. It is the map ℤ → H̃₀(S⁰; ℤ) that sends 1 to the class [false] − [true]. This comes from the docstring and from the way it is used as a basis paired with `twoPointReducedCoordinate`.
explanation:
Here `reducedSingularHomologyZero` is the kernel of the augmentation ε : H₀(X; ℤ) → ℤ. `twoPointReducedBasisClass` is the difference of the two point classes, `singularHomologyZeroPoint false - singularHomologyZeroPoint true`. The lemma `twoPointReducedBasisClass_augmentation` shows this difference is killed by ε. So `kernel.lift` gives exactly the map ℤ → H̃₀(S⁰) with 1 ↦ [false] − [true], as the docstring says.

The companion lemmas `twoPointReducedBasis_coordinate` and `twoPointReducedCoordinate_basis` prove that this map is an isomorphism. So it really is a basis vector, i.e. a generator of H̃₀(S⁰) ≅ ℤ.

This is a specific object, a chosen generator for one specific space, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no counterpart.
